title: Language Models Embody and Amplify Human Cognitive Distortions: What is to be Done?

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating explicit preferences by asking models if they prefer white over Black people, and assessing covert racial bias by comparing model decisions (such as job assignment, conviction, and sentencing) when presented with identical content in African American English versus Standard American English.
Measuring models' covert stereotyping and discriminatory judgments by varying the dialect of input text (Standard American English compared to African American English).
Testing explicit bias benchmarks by asking models directly whether they prefer thin people over fat people.
Asking models to evaluate written work to observe whether they rate their own outputs or LLM-generated content more highly than human-generated text or the outputs of other models.
Evaluating models' selection decisions based on false inferences about traits like trust and competence derived solely from face morphology.

Testing language models on classic reasoning tasks from psychology to observe if they reproduce human cognitive distortions and are susceptible to persuasion, propaganda, and tactics involving authority, scarcity, and affiliation.

bias_targets.target: Multiple demographic biases (Gender, Age, Disability, Ethnicity, Religion, Sexual orientation)
bias_targets.methodology: Summarizing existing behavioral audits and literature that test models using both explicit benchmarks and implicit association measures across various protected social categories.
